explanation:
Let $A:K^C\to K^R$ be the surjective matrix map in the statement. We prove

$$
\exists s:R\to C,\qquad s\text{ injective},\qquad \det\bigl(A[\operatorname{id}_R,s]\bigr)\ne0.
$$

Choose a matrix right inverse $B$, so $AB=I_R$ and hence $\det(AB)=1$. Expanding this determinant in Cauchy--Binet form gives a finite sum over functions $p:R\to C$:

$$
\det(AB)=\sum_{p:R\to C} \det\bigl(A[\operatorname{id}_R,p]\bigr)\prod_{i\in R}B_{p(i),i}.
$$

Because the sum equals $1$, at least one summand is nonzero, and its matrix minor therefore has nonzero determinant. If its column selector identified two different rows, the square minor would have two equal columns and zero determinant. The selector is consequently injective.
natural_language_statement:
Let $R$ and $C$ be finite index types, let $K$ be a field, and let $A=(A_{r,c})_{r\in R,\,c\in C}$ be an $R$-by-$C$ matrix over $K$. Assume equality on $R$ is decidable and multiplication by $A$ defines a surjective $K$-linear map $K^C\to K^R$. Then there is a function $s:R\to C$ such that $s$ is injective and

$$
\det\bigl(A[\operatorname{id}_R,s]\bigr)\ne 0.
$$

Thus the selected columns form a nonsingular square minor containing every row. This generic matrix-rank lemma is a direct core dependency for choosing a nonvanishing interpolation minor in the $\pi$ irrationality-measure argument.

source_witness.mathematical_role: Generic finite matrix-rank lemma and direct core dependency for the nonsingular interpolation minor used by OpenAI math family 017.

theorem_title: A surjective matrix has a nonsingular full-row minor
